provenance: Sample output: these assessments were hand-written to illustrate the agent's output format and were replayed through the same validation guardrails. They were not produced by a live AI run.
summary: CloudNova is at an early maturity stage for NIS2. Technical basics exist (SSO with MFA for staff, TLS, CloudTrail, daily snapshots), but governance, incident management and reporting are largely missing. The three most urgent gaps are: (1) no incident response or NIS2 reporting process, so the 24h/72h deadlines would be missed; (2) no MFA on the AWS root account and shared admin credentials; (3) no approved security policy or management-body oversight, which NIS2 makes a personal accountability issue for leadership.

assessments.rationale: No approved security policy (E-01) and the board has not discussed cyber risk or received training in 12 months (E-02).
assessments.gap: Management body neither approves nor oversees cybersecurity measures and has no training.
assessments.recommendation: Have the board formally approve the security policy and risk treatment plan, add a quarterly cyber-risk agenda item, and schedule NIS2 training for all directors.

assessments.rationale: A first ISO 27005 risk register exists (E-03) but it is not approved, the security guideline is an unapproved draft (E-01) and the asset inventory is incomplete (E-04).
assessments.gap: Risk analysis is not formalised, approved or tied to a complete asset inventory.
assessments.recommendation: Approve the risk register with a treatment plan and owners, finalise the security policy, and extend the inventory to cloud resources and data stores.

assessments.rationale: Incidents are handled ad hoc in Slack with no plan or roles (E-16); logs exist but are not reviewed and no security alerts are configured (E-15).
assessments.gap: No incident response plan, defined roles or detection capability.
assessments.recommendation: Write an incident response plan with roles and severity levels, configure security alerts on CloudTrail/CloudWatch, and run a tabletop exercise.

assessments.rationale: Daily snapshots and a multi-AZ database exist (E-11, E-17), but restores were never tested, RPO/RTO are undefined and there is no DR plan for a region outage.
assessments.gap: Backups are untested and there is no continuity, DR or crisis-management plan.
assessments.recommendation: Define RPO/RTO, perform and document a quarterly restore test, and write a DR plan covering a full AWS region outage.

assessments.rationale: Suppliers are selected on price and features only, with no security assessment or clauses (E-20).
assessments.gap: No supplier security assessment, contractual clauses or list of critical suppliers.
assessments.recommendation: Identify critical suppliers, send a short security questionnaire, and add security and incident-notification clauses to contracts.

assessments.rationale: Peer review on pull requests and a 2024 pentest exist (E-12, E-13), but there is no SAST/DAST, no dependency scanning, irregular patching and no vulnerability scanner (E-14).
assessments.gap: Secure development and vulnerability handling are not systematic.
assessments.recommendation: Add SAST and dependency scanning to CI/CD, adopt a vulnerability scanner with patch SLAs, retest the 2024 pentest findings and publish a vulnerability disclosure contact.

assessments.rationale: No security metrics are tracked and no internal audit has been performed (E-24).
assessments.gap: No way to measure whether security measures are effective.
assessments.recommendation: Define 5–8 security KPIs (e.g. MFA coverage, patch latency, restore-test success) and plan an annual internal audit.

assessments.rationale: Onboarding includes a short security video (E-19) and most laptops are managed and encrypted (E-18), but there is no refresher training, no phishing simulation, no EDR and contractor devices are unmanaged.
assessments.gap: Training is one-off and cyber hygiene does not cover all devices.
assessments.recommendation: Introduce annual training with phishing simulations, extend MDM to 100% of devices used for work (including contractors) and deploy EDR.

assessments.rationale: TLS 1.2+ and KMS-managed keys are in place (E-22), but not all S3 buckets are encrypted (E-10) and there is no cryptography policy.
assessments.gap: Encryption is applied inconsistently and not governed by a policy.
assessments.recommendation: Write a short cryptography policy, enforce default encryption on all S3 buckets and review KMS key rotation settings.

assessments.rationale: Shared admin accounts and AdministratorAccess roles (E-05), no offboarding (E-07), no access reviews (E-08) and an incomplete asset inventory (E-04).
assessments.gap: Access control, HR security and asset management do not meet basic requirements.
assessments.recommendation: Remove shared accounts, apply least privilege in AWS IAM, introduce an offboarding checklist with same-day access removal, and run quarterly access reviews.

assessments.rationale: MFA is enforced for staff Google Workspace/SSO (E-06), but not on the AWS root account (E-05), not offered to customers (E-09), and there is no emergency communication channel (E-23).
assessments.gap: MFA is missing on the most privileged account and for customers; no secured emergency communications.
assessments.recommendation: Enable MFA on the AWS root account immediately, offer MFA to customer users, and set up an out-of-band emergency contact channel.

assessments.rationale: The team is not aware of the 24h/72h NIS2 deadlines (E-16) and there is no breach-notification procedure (E-21).
assessments.gap: No process to classify significant incidents and notify the authority within NIS2 deadlines.
assessments.recommendation: Add a reporting annex to the incident plan with significance criteria, the competent CSIRT contact and templates for the 24h warning, 72h notification and one-month final report.
